jurisdiction.name: Estonia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Estonia steers AI mainly through non-binding plans: the national AI action plans (the current 2024-2026 plan) and the Data and AI White Paper 2024-2030, supported by a public-sector toolkit on procurement, project checklists, algorithm transparency and an AI sandbox concept. The Ministry of Defence published an AI strategy in 2025, the education ministry has guidance for schools, and a 2025 school-law amendment gives schools a legal basis to process pupils' data in AI applications. The data protection inspectorate has issued AI guidance; a law implementing the EU AI Act was not found.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. One existing record turned out to be Estonia's position on an EU consultation rather than a national instrument and was removed, and the AI Act implementing law could not be found.

instruments.official_title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Estonia
instruments.english_title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Estonia
instruments.summary: Estonia's first defence AI strategy for institutions in the Ministry of Defence's area of governance, aiming at direct military advantage (decision support, intelligence, targeting), more efficient support services and a stronger local defence industry. It sets five lines of action (a digital and technology development unit in the Defence Forces, digital infrastructure and data standards, AI skills, civil cooperation, allied interoperability), ethical and legal principles including NATO's principles of responsible use, and systematic AI adoption by 2030 with reviews at least every two years.
instruments.current_status: Announced by the Ministry on 24 March 2025; document dated Tallinn 2025; ministry page last updated 15.04.2026.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext); policy page links this PDF; publication date from the ministry news item of 24.03.2025 (kaitseministeerium.ee/en/news/ministry-defence-unveils-defence-artificial-intelligence-strategy).

instruments.english_title: Report of the Estonian expert group on the adoption of artificial intelligence (kratt report)
instruments.issuing_authority: Expert group on AI adoption convened by the Government Office (Strategy Unit) and the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
instruments.summary: Report of the 'kratt' expert group commissioned by the Government Office's strategy unit, reviewing AI technologies, international AI plans and Estonia's position. It sets out proposals for an Estonian action plan for AI adoption in the public and private sectors, R&D and education, and the legal changes needed (including the 'kratt' legislative package), and was the basis of the first national AI action plan 2019-2021.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding analysis of Estonia's AI policy; the 2019-2021 kratikava grew out of it.
instruments.current_status: Published May 2019 and listed on kratid.ee ('Visioon ja kavad') as the 2019 expert group report; historical. The 2019-2021 action plan itself is referred to in later plans but its stand-alone text was not found on an official site (see leads).
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext); cover states 'Mai 2019', commissioned by the Government Office strategy unit; linked from kratid.ee/kratt-visioon.

instruments.official_title: Eesti riiklik tehisintellekti alane tegevuskava ehk kratikava 2022-2023
instruments.english_title: Estonian national artificial intelligence action plan ('kratikava') 2022-2023
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
instruments.summary: Second national AI action plan, continuing the 2019-2021 kratikava (budget about EUR 10 million) and reporting that over 80 public-sector kratt projects had been run. It sets measures for 2022-2023 in five areas: public sector, private sector, R&D and education, data as an enabler, and the legal environment, including human-centric and trustworthy AI principles.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Superseded national AI strategy, kept for the timeline.
instruments.current_status: Dated 'Majandus- ja Kommunikatsiooniministeerium 2021'; superseded by the AI action plan 2024-2026, which describes itself as continuing the 2019-2021 and 2022-2023 plans.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Education and Research
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
instruments.summary: Third national AI action plan, which it states is also Estonia's national AI strategy within the meaning of the EU Coordinated Plan on AI and which implements the Data and AI White Paper 2024-2030. With SWOT analyses and strategic goals it sets actions for the public sector, private sector, R&D and education and the legal environment, noting that over 130 AI projects had been run in more than 65 public organisations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy and action plan.
instruments.current_status: Current plan per kratid.ee ('Hetkel lähtutakse ... tegevuskavast aastateks 2024-2026'). A 47-page version is on mkm.ee and a designed 75-page version on kratid.ee. A successor strategy under the Government Office's Eesti.ai initiative is reported but no official text was found (see leads).

instruments.english_title: Data and Artificial Intelligence White Paper 2024-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs (prepared under the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Medium-term (seven-year) strategic document for data and AI that sets goals for 2024-2030 and bridges the sectoral development plans and the short-term data and AI action plans. It covers three sub-areas: putting data to work, 'AI in every corner' of state and society (education, public sector, private sector, language technology, R&D) and human-centric, trustworthy data and AI, including the legal environment and international cooperation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Umbrella strategy that the AI action plan 2024-2026 implements; source of the algorithm-transparency goals.
instruments.current_status: Published 2024 and listed first under 'Dokumendid' on kratid.ee/kratt-visioon; cited by the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs' 2026 sandbox concept as 'Justiits- ja Digiministeerium, 2024'.

instruments.english_title: Guidance material on procuring AI ('kratt') solutions
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (kratid.ee programme)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Guidance for public-sector bodies on procuring AI and data-science projects. Its recommendations include treating a pilot's result as knowledge, describing problems rather than fixing one solution, giving bidders an overview of available data, taking account of the market, allowing cloud computing and iterative scope changes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Estonia's AI procurement guidance for public bodies.
instruments.current_status: Dated November 2019; still listed under 'Tehisintellektiga seotud juhised' on kratid.ee/juhised.

instruments.english_title: Algorithm use overview (public-sector algorithm transparency form)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications / Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Form with 19 mandatory questions for public-sector bodies to describe AI and other algorithmic systems that may affect people's rights, freedoms or duties (automated administrative acts, decision support, profiling, chatbots such as Bürokratt, LLM use). Completed forms are sent to the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs and published on kratid.ee as the basis of a future public-sector algorithm register.

instruments.official_title: Tehisaru testkeskkond: usaldusväärse ja õiguspärase tehisaru arendamine ning rakendamine
instruments.english_title: AI testing environment (sandbox): developing and deploying trustworthy and lawful AI - concept
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Concept (version 1.5) for a national AI testing environment combining regulatory support (legal and compliance advice, risk assessment, data protection) and technical testing for public and private organisations, including high-risk systems, in line with the EU AI Act's regulatory sandbox duty. It sets the operating model, parties, participation and operator selection, final reports, the link to the experimentation framework, and next steps including an algorithm register (March 2026), AI Act implementing-law amendments (planned June 2026) and launch of the sandbox service.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Estonia's AI regulatory sandbox design under the AI Act.
instruments.current_status: Version 1.5, January 2026, linked from kratid.ee/testkeskkond. Whether the planned implementing-law amendments were adopted could not be confirmed (see leads).
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): 13-page PDF read (pdftotext); 'Versioon 1.5 | Jaanuar 2026', author Ott Velsberg; linked from kratid.ee/testkeskkond.

instruments.english_title: AI guide for school leaders, teachers and students
instruments.summary: Ministry guide encouraging schools to treat AI (including chatbots) as a chance to rethink teaching materials and methods, with recommendations for school leaders, teachers and students. It stresses purposeful, ethical (data-protection compliant) and critical use of AI, and was drafted by a working group of ministry, university, school and student representatives.

instruments.official_title: Põhikooli- ja gümnaasiumiseaduse ning kutseõppeasutuse seaduse muutmise seadus (direktorite atesteerimine, õpetajate karjäärimudel ning isikuandmete töötlemine tehisintellekti rakenduse kasutamisel)
instruments.english_title: Act amending the Basic Schools and Upper Secondary Schools Act and the Vocational Educational Institutions Act (certification of principals, teacher career model and processing of personal data when using AI applications)
instruments.summary: Act adopted by the Riigikogu on 17 December 2025 that, besides principals' certification and a teacher career model, gives schools a legal basis to process pupils' personal data (including special categories) for using AI applications in teaching. Per the committee amendment text, data may be kept up to three months after the pupil leaves, the application must let pupils delete data they entered, and the minister may set further safeguards by regulation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Estonia's first statutory AI-specific provision, underpinning the AI Leap (TI-Hüpe) programme in schools.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 17.12.2025 and promulgated by President's decision no. 647 of 23.12.2025. The final Riigi Teataja text, section number (§ 20¹ in the committee's amendment) and entry-into-force date were not verified because the Riigi Teataja site requires JavaScript.

instruments.english_title: Notice drawing attention: use of general-purpose AI in healthcare
instruments.summary: Data Protection Inspectorate letter no. 2.2-10/26/1922-1 to a healthcare provider, prompted by a social-media post, explaining GDPR principles for processing health data when using a general-purpose AI tool such as ChatGPT. It distinguishes free consumer from business-licensed versions, notes that even business versions may not ensure compliance for health data, and covers legal basis, minimisation, retention and security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulator's position on generative AI use with health data.
instruments.current_status: Issued 07.05.2026; published in the AKI 'tehisaru' (AI and data protection) section together with a 16.04.2026 reply on AI-based clinical documentation software.

leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs
leads.note: The JDM sandbox concept (v1.5, Jan 2026) plans AI Act implementing-law amendments entering into force in early June 2026 (sandbox service, real-world testing of high-risk systems, roles). kratid.ee/tehisintellektimaarus says MKM and the Ministry of Justice designated AKI, the Gender Equality and Equal Treatment Commissioner and TTJA as Article 77 bodies (undated web page). No bill found in EIS / Riigikogu / Riigi Teataja searches (Riigi Teataja search needs JavaScript). Re-check market surveillance authority designation.
